title: Travel Vocabulary
summary: Pack, fold, highway, boarding area — travel English (Premium).
script:
Hi! Today you're making tea for yourself.
You're getting ready to travel.
While you drink your tea, you're packing your bag.
To pack your bag means to put the things you need into your bag, usually because you're getting ready to go somewhere.
You're carefully folding your clothes and putting them in your bag.
To fold means to make clothes smaller by putting one part over another.
You zip up your bag, and now you're ready to go.
You put your bag in the car and take the highway to the airport.
Listen. You can hear the cars on the highway.
A highway is a big road that connects places, where cars usually drive fast.
There's not much traffic today.
You arrive at the airport and park your car in the parking lot.
You roll your suitcase to the check-in counter.
To roll your suitcase means to move your suitcase using its wheels.
You arrive at the check-in counter and check your bag.
Listen. This is the sound of the conveyor belt.
The conveyor belt is a long, moving surface that carries your checked bag toward the plane.
You patiently walk to the boarding area to find your gate.
The boarding area is the part of the airport where passengers wait near their gate before getting on the plane.
They're calling your flight. It's time to board the plane and enjoy your calm flight.
Enjoy it. Bye!

vocabulary.definition: to put the things you need into your bag before a trip
to make clothes smaller by putting one part over another
a big road that connects places, where cars usually travel fast
the part of an airport where passengers wait before getting on the plane

exercises.sentence: Before you leave, remember _____ with your clothes and travel documents.
